items.title: deleting an api key or changing a role: how long until it takes effect?
items.body:
i'm about to put an api key in a storefront, so i checked what revoking one looks like if it leaks.

the tree has `src/lib/permissions/cache.ts` and the cache adapters (`memory.ts`, `redis.ts`, `cloudflare-kv.ts`). that makes me think key and role lookups are cached. i couldn't find anything that says when the cache gets invalidated:

- when i delete a key under **Settings → API Keys** (`DELETE /api/settings/api-keys/[id]`), is it rejected on the very next request to `/admin/api/2024-01/graphql.json`, or does it keep working until a TTL runs out?
- same question for editing a role's features (`/api/settings/roles/[id]/features`) or changing a user's role (`/api/settings/users/[id]/role`). does an already logged-in session pick up the change right away?
- with the in-memory adapter on node and more than one instance running, does a revoke on one instance clear the others?
- on workers with KV, reads are eventually consistent across locations (up to about 60s). is a revoked key expected to keep working at other locations during that window?

if there's a TTL, it'd help to know the value, and whether a revoked key keeping access for that long is intended.

items.title: (bug) Role and membership changes take up to 5 minutes to take effect

labels.name: python
labels.description: Pull requests that update Python code

items.body:
When I change a member's role or remove them from a project, I expect the change to take effect immediately: the code invalidates the permission cache on every role and membership change. Instead, the invalidation silently deletes nothing, and the old cached answers (positive and negative) keep being served until the cache TTL expires. Net effect: **every role and membership change takes up to 5 minutes to apply, for all permissions, product-wide.** Found during an internal code audit; verified on current `main` (`bc2481b2cc`).

## What happens

1. Permission checks are cached per `(project_id, user_id, permission)` with a 5-minute TTL, including negative results: [`api/oss/src/core/access/permissions/service.py:197-227`](https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta/blob/bc2481b2cc473c07aaca1bd9666b40a5e4f4a1cc/api/oss/src/core/access/permissions/service.py#L197-L227).
2. Every role/membership change calls `invalidate_cache(namespace="check_action_access", project_id=...)` **without** a `user_id`: [`api/oss/src/services/db_manager.py:854`](https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta/blob/bc2481b2cc473c07aaca1bd9666b40a5e4f4a1cc/api/oss/src/services/db_manager.py#L854), [`:948`](https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta/blob/bc2481b2cc473c07aaca1bd9666b40a5e4f4a1cc/api/oss/src/services/db_manager.py#L948), [`:1227`](https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta/blob/bc2481b2cc473c07aaca1bd9666b40a5e4f4a1cc/api/oss/src/services/db_manager.py#L1227), [`:1694`](https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta/blob/bc2481b2cc473c07aaca1bd9666b40a5e4f4a1cc/api/oss/src/services/db_manager.py#L1694).
3. In `_pack` ([`api/oss/src/utils/caching.py:43-75`](https://github.com/Agenta-AI/agenta/blob/bc2481b2cc473c07aaca1bd9666b40a5e4f4a1cc/api/oss/src/utils/caching.py#L43-L75)), `pattern=True` turns an omitted `namespace` and `key` into `*` wildcards (lines 62-64), but an omitted `user_id` is padded to a literal `------------` segment (lines 56-60) instead of a wildcard. Cached entries carry the real user id in that segment, so the scan pattern never matches any cached entry.

Replaying `_pack` shows the written key vs the invalidation scan pattern:

```
written key : cache:p:6c1d2e3f4a5b:u:9c0d1e2f3a4b:check_action_access:controls:abc123:permission:run_service:role:None
scan pattern: cache:p:6c1d2e3f4a5b:u:------------:check_action_access:*
matches     : False
```

Since these four call sites are the only RBAC cache invalidations, every one of them is a no-op.

## Observable symptoms

- Downgrading or removing a member: they keep their old permissions for up to 5 minutes.
- Upgrading a member or adding them to a project: they keep getting denied for up to 5 minutes, and because each `(permission)` entry is cached independently on first use, the denials are asymmetric — e.g. a newly promoted member can create a resource (fresh "yes") but not list it (stale cached "no") within the same window.

## Fix sketch

In `_pack`, when `pattern=True` and `user_id` is omitted, emit `*` for the user segment, mirroring the existing `namespace`/`key` handling. Add a regression test asserting that `invalidate_cache(namespace=..., project_id=...)` actually removes an entry written with a `user_id`.

items.title: Member role changes do not take effect until the target's access token refreshes, and the console role change writes a different table from the one the claim reads

labels.name: priority:high
labels.description: Needed before demo, not blocking today.

labels.name: demo-surface
labels.description: Visible to the owner or a customer during the demo walk.

milestone.title: Hive Enterprise edge-first v1
milestone.description: Enterprise edge-first v1: self-hosted data plane parity, sovereignty posture, security P0 family resolved, backups operational, admin/RBC hardening. Exit criteria: box deployable end-to-end from fresh clone with off-box backups running.

items.body:
## Summary

Authorization role is read from a JWT claim that is baked at token issue time, so a role change cannot take effect until the target user's access token is refreshed. A demoted owner keeps OWNER authority for the remaining lifetime of their current access token. Separately, and more seriously, the console's member role change writes a different table from the one the claim is derived from, so on the evidence in the repository the console role change never reaches the claim at all.

## Evidence, part one: the claim is a snapshot

* `supabase/migrations/20260726_01_owui_role_claim.sql:115` — the access token hook writes `jsonb_build_object('role', user_role)` into the token claims.
* `user_role` is pinned to a single snapshot of `public.tenant_users` taken at token issue time. See the `active_memberships` CTE at `:69` to `:90` of the same file.
* Row level security reads that claim directly, in every policy that grants elevated access:
  * `supabase/migrations/20260516_03_phase19_tenant_users.sql:38,46,50,58`
  * `supabase/migrations/20260516_02_phase19_tenant_settings.sql:59,67,71,79`
  * `supabase/migrations/20260518_04_phase19_audit_rls_and_indexes.sql:194,203,207,216,232,241,245,254`
  * All of the form `(auth.jwt() ->> 'role') IN ('OWNER','ADMIN')`.
* Go side trusts the same claim: `apps/edge-api/internal/auth/jwt_supabase.go:132` reads `role` off the token and lowercases it for the authz policy table.

So the window is the full remaining lifetime of the issued access token. The repository does not pin a JWT expiry, so this is the Supabase default (one hour) unless the project overrides it. During that window a demoted owner retains read and write access to `tenant_users`, `tenant_settings`, and the audit tables, including the ability to re-promote themselves through `tenant_users`, which would extend the window indefinitely. Revoking a membership has the same lag.

Not every path is affected. Some server side checks read the database rather than the claim, for example `platform.GetTenantRole` (`apps/control-plane/internal/platform/role_pgx.go:76`), which queries `public.tenant_users` directly. Those are correct today and are the model for the fix.

## Evidence, part two: the console role change writes a different table

The staleness above assumes the new role eventually lands in `public.tenant_users`. On the code in the repository, it does not.

* The operator surface is `PATCH /api/v1/accounts/current/members/{user_id}` (`apps/control-plane/internal/accounts/http.go:206`, path prefix at `:368`), which reaches `apps/control-plane/internal/accounts/service.go:401` and then `apps/control-plane/internal/accounts/repository.go:212`.
* That statement updates `public.account_memberships` (`repository.go:214`). It does not touch `public.tenant_users`.
* The access token hook derives `role` from `public.tenant_users` (`supabase/migrations/20260726_01_owui_role_claim.sql:71`).
* There is no `UPDATE` against `public.tenant_users` anywhere in production Go or SQL. The only writes are inserts: `apps/control-plane/internal/signup/personal_tenant.go:157` and `apps/control-plane/internal/signup/reconcile.go:252`, both `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, the latter hardcoding `'MEMBER'`. No trigger or migration synchronizes `account_memberships` to `tenant_users`.

If that reading is right, a demotion performed in the console changes the account level role while the RLS facing tenant role stays at whatever it was at provisioning time, permanently, not just for a token lifetime. This should be confirmed against a live database before the fix is designed, because it changes the remedy: a token revocation on role change fixes the staleness but does nothing about a role change that never reaches the claim's source table.

## Proposed remedies

Pick both, in this order.

1. **Stop trusting the claim for authorization decisions.** Route elevated checks through a server side role read against the source of truth, the way `platform.GetTenantRole` (`apps/control-plane/internal/platform/role_pgx.go:76`) already does. For RLS this means replacing `(auth.jwt() ->> 'role')` with a security definer function that reads `public.tenant_users` for the current user and tenant. This removes the window entirely rather than shrinking it, and it is the only remedy that survives an attacker who simply avoids refreshing their token.
2. **Revoke sessions on role change.** On a successful demotion or membership revocation, invalidate the target user's refresh token and sessions so the next request forces a fresh token. This is a defence in depth measure and is not sufficient alone, because it does not bound an already issued access token unless the access token lifetime is also reduced.

Additionally, reconcile the two role tables. Either the console role change must write `public.tenant_users` as well, or the two role concepts must be documented as distinct with an explicit statement of which one authorizes what.

## Acceptance

1. A test that demotes an active owner and asserts the demoted user is refused on an RLS protected write, using the token issued before the demotion.
2. A test that asserts a console role change is visible in whatever table the authorization decision reads from.

items.title: JWT `role` claim trusted without DB equivalence — role changes and bans don't take effect

labels.name: Stellar Wave
labels.description: Issues in the Stellar wave program

items.body:
## Context
`backend/src/middleware/auth.js`; `backend/src/routes/auth.js:92-97`; `.env.example JWT_EXPIRES_IN=7d`.

## Problem
`requireRole` reads `req.user.role` from the signed token payload; the DB row is only consulted for flags. Role demotions/promotions and bans don't take effect until token expiry (up to 7 days).

## Impact
Revoked privileges persist for up to a week.

## Suggested solution
Re-read authoritative role/flags from DB per request (or short-lived tokens + refresh), and enforce `is_banned` server-side.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Demotion/bannation takes effect within one request
- [ ] Role/flag policy enforced from DB on every request
- [ ] Tests for role change propagation

items.title: fix(bracket): Game Changer removals take effect, and check_bracket counts roles like the page
items.body:
## Why

**Game Changer removals never took effect.** `liveGetGameChangerNames` returned the union of the hardcoded list and Scryfall's live `is:gamechanger` query. When the RC removes a card (ten in October 2025), the hardcoded copy kept flooring it until someone edited the code.

**The AI `check_bracket` tool drifted from the page.**
- Its role counts included lands and commanders, with no oracle-text evidence check.
- Its average mana value included the commander.

The page counts roles over mainboard non-lands, checks each against the card's own text, and leaves commanders out of both. The tool reports a before/after change, but its absolute "Before: bracket N" could still contradict what the user was looking at.

## Changes

- **Game Changer list:** a complete live fetch is authoritative. The hardcoded list is only a fallback when page 1 fails, or a floor unioned into a partial fetch when pagination breaks mid-way, so a missing page can't undercount. A debug log names any hardcoded card the live list no longer has, so a stale copy shows up.
- **Role evidence:** the `ROLE_EVIDENCE` rule moved into `packages/deck-metrics` as `checkRoleEvidence`. The frontend's `validateCardRole` calls it, unchanged in signature and behavior. `taglookup-parity` and `commanderDeckAnalysis` stay green, and the page's output is unchanged, so there's no engine bump.
- **Backend `estimateForNames`:**
  - skips lands and commanders for role counts and the average mana value;
  - gates each role against the cached card's oracle text (front face for multi-face cards);
  - still sends commanders to combo matching.

## Guards

- `gamechangers.test.ts`:
  - a complete live list drops a hardcoded card it lacks;
  - a page-1 failure gives exactly the hardcoded list;
  - a page-2 failure keeps the hardcoded floor.
- `bracket.test.ts`:
  - a land with a tagger role adds no interaction;
  - a tagged card without the evidence text adds none;
  - the commander's mana value is left out of the average.
- `roleEvidence.test.ts` covers the moved rule.

## Gate

- `deck-metrics`: typecheck, format, coverage (117 tests).
- Backend: typecheck, lint, format, and full `test:coverage` (113 files, 1,927 tests).
- Frontend: typecheck, eslint, stylelint, format, and full `test:coverage` (855 files).
- The shared-package registration check passes.

After rebasing onto #2207, both typechecks pass.

items.title: Change user's role from `User` to `User Light` after the user has logged in takes no effect.
items.body:
## Describe the bug

Change user's role from `User` to `User Light` after the user has logged in takes no effect.

When the user is set as `User Light` before the first login, the user will not have personal space. I think this is what it's expected.
However, if we change the user's role from `User` to `User Light` after the user has logged then nothing will happen. The user will still has its personal space and can still upload files.

The role of the user DOES have changed. If it is not allowed to change the role after the user's first login, warning should be given to the admin. If it is allowed, the user with the new role `User Light` new role should no longer be able to upload.

## Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create a new user with role set as `User`.
2. Login with the new user, we can see the personal space.
3. Change the user's role to `User Light`, login again with the user. The personal space is still there and files can be uploaded.

## Expected behavior
The user with the new role `User Light` new role should no longer be able to upload.

## Actual behavior
The user still has its personal space and can still upload files.

## Setup
- ocis: 3.1.0-next.2+038520778
- web: 7.0.1

items.title: [backend/auth] refreshToken() re-issues tokens from the old token's claims — role changes, org reassignment, deactivation and soft-deletion never take effect for an existing session

labels.name: Stellar Wave
labels.description: Issues in the Stellar wave program

items.body:
**Location:** `backend/src/auth/auth.service.ts:427-449` (`refreshToken`), `:108-132` (`login`)

**Description:** On rotation, new tokens are built solely from the presented refresh token's payload; the user row is never reloaded:

```ts
const newPayload: JwtPayload = {
  sub: payload.sub, email: payload.email, role: payload.role,
  sid: payload.sid, organizationId: payload.organizationId ?? null,
};
```

Each refresh mints a new 7-day refresh token and extends the session, so a session lives indefinitely with whatever role and `organizationId` it had at login:
- A user demoted from `admin`/`hospital` or moved to another organization keeps the old privileges and tenant scope.
- A user soft-deleted via `DELETE /users/:id` (`users.service.ts:136-149`, which does not revoke sessions) keeps refreshing.
- `UserEntity.isActive` (`user.entity.ts:84-85`) is not checked by `login()` either, so deactivated accounts can log in and refresh.

**Fix:** load the user in `refreshToken()`, reject missing/soft-deleted/inactive users, and take `role`/`organizationId` from the database; check `isActive` in `login()`.

items.title: Role change doesn't take effect until re-login — new tutor's dashboard 403s on every action

labels.name: S2
labels.description: Key flow broken or wrong result

labels.name: qa-found
labels.description: Surfaced by the QA audit sweep

items.body:
**Severity:** S2

### Symptom
After a tutor request is approved (or any admin role change), the web app routes the user to their new dashboard, but every `/tenant/*` API call returns 403 until they log out and back in — or until the 7-day JWT expires. It self-heals on re-login, so it rarely reproduces when you go looking for it.

### Evidence
- `apps/api/src/middleware/auth.middleware.ts:35-44` — role is backfilled from the DB only when `!payload.role` (legacy tokens). A current token carrying a stale role passes through unchanged.
- `apps/api/src/controllers/auth.controller.ts:210-211` — `me()` reissues a token only for legacy tokens.
- `apps/web/components/session-sync.tsx:23` — keeps the existing token.

### Reproduction
1. As an INDIVIDUAL, request tutor upgrade.
2. As ADMIN, approve it with a seat limit.
3. As that user, reload the web app without logging out.
4. `/auth/me` reports TENANT_OWNER and the UI routes to `/tenant/dashboard`, but every panel 403s.

### Notes
Already logged in the QA ledger as **F45**.

---
Surfaced by the QA-system audit of 2026-08-24. These came from the previously **unverified** "Suspected findings ledger (code-read)" in `docs/qa/user-stories-expansion.md:3238` — 55 hypotheses that were never verified or promoted. Each was re-checked against the current working tree and adversarially re-verified; 15 turned out to be already fixed and 4 were wrong. This one is **live**.

items.title: Role changes take up to 7 days to take effect
items.body:
Bug: **Role changes take up to 7 days to take effect**. Part of Theme #29. Blocks Epic #30.

Role claims are snapshotted into the auth cookie at Discord sign-in and never refreshed.
An admin granting or revoking a role sees no effect until that user's cookie expires.

## Detail

`backend/src/NajaEcho.Api/Program.cs:181-200` reads the user's roles once, during
`OnTicketReceived`, and bakes them into the `ClaimsIdentity`:

```csharp
var userRoles = appUser is not null ? await userManager.GetRolesAsync(appUser) : [];
var roleClaims = userRoles.Select(r => new Claim(ClaimTypes.Role, r));
var identity = new ClaimsIdentity([...roleClaims], IdentityConstants.ApplicationScheme);
```

`OnValidatePrincipal` (`Program.cs:92-101`) enforces only a 7-day absolute cap — it never
re-reads roles from the database. The cookie is 24h sliding, so an active user renews
indefinitely up to that 7-day ceiling.

`SignInManager` is deliberately unused (see `002-identity-refactor`), so the stock
`ValidateSecurityStamp` revalidation is not wired up.

## Impact

- **Revocation is the sharp edge.** A removed Quartermaster keeps write access to
  warehouse endpoints for up to 7 days.
- Granting is merely confusing: the admin assigns a role, the user sees nothing change,
  and neither has a signal explaining why.
- `UserRepository.SetRolesAsync` (`Infrastructure/Identity/UserRepository.cs:57`) does
  remove-all-then-add, so *every* role edit republishes the full set — a no-op edit still
  leaves the cookie stale relative to the DB.

Tolerable for three slow-moving roles. It scales badly as roles become situational, and
#31 makes org membership another cookie-resident fact with the same staleness.

## Repro

1. Sign in as a user holding `Quartermaster`.
2. As an admin, remove that role via `PUT /api/admin/users/{id}/roles`.
3. As the first user, without signing out, `POST /api/warehouse/items`.
4. Request succeeds. Expected: 403.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Given** an admin revokes a role, **when** the affected user makes their next
  request, **then** the role no longer authorizes them.
- **Given** an admin grants a role, **when** the affected user reloads,
  **then** `GET /api/auth/me` reflects the new role without a sign-out.
- **Given** a user whose roles are unchanged, **when** they browse normally, **then**
  the fix does not add a database round-trip to every request.

## Approach options

Cheapest correct fix is enabling security-stamp revalidation on cookie validation —
`UserManager.UpdateSecurityStampAsync` on role change, and a `ValidatePrincipal` that
rejects a stale stamp. Interval-based revalidation trades a bounded staleness window for
fewer lookups. Rebuilding claims on every validate is simplest but puts a user+roles
query on the hot path.

Decision belongs in `/speckit-plan`.

items.title: Reissue the token on 403 so a role change takes effect (v1.23.1)
items.body:
A Catalyst Center token carries the account's role **at issue time**, and the client caches one for ~55 minutes. Granting the API account provisioning rights would otherwise keep failing with 403 until the cached token aged out — the change would appear to do nothing.

`_request` now forces one token reissue on **403** as well as 401. A 403 that survives a fresh token is reported as what it is — the account's role, not a stale token — naming System → Users & Roles.

## Verification

- 249 pytest, 39 vitest, 4 Playwright e2e green
- `ruff` / `ruff format` / `mypy --strict` / `eslint` / `prettier` clean
- Tests cover both the recovery path (403 → refresh → success) and the genuine role failure

items.title: Role/access changes take effect immediately (no re-login)
items.body:
Follow-up to #113/#114. When an admin reassigned a user's role (including to a custom role), the user's open session didn't update — it looked empty until a full reload.

**Root cause:** the profile realtime handler called `setProfile(role)` but never re-pulled the **role-keyed** module map (`get_user_module_permissions`), so the new role resolved against the *old* role's stale perms.

**AuthContext fix:**
- On a profile update, also call `refreshAccess()` (via a ref) so the module map / grants / capabilities re-pull for the **new** role immediately.
- On tab refocus, also re-pull the user's own profile (role/site/country/approval) alongside `refreshAccess`, so a role reassignment takes full effect on next focus even if realtime isn't delivering profile events. Never toggles `loading`; lock/approval revocation still ends the session.

**Instant path (migration):** module-level custom-role edits already propagate live (`module_permissions` is published, V227). Role *reassignment* didn't, because `profiles` was never in the realtime publication. **`MIGRATIONS_V280`** adds `public.profiles` to `supabase_realtime` so the existing per-user profile subscription fires and a role change is instant (RLS still scopes each client to its own row).

> ⚠️ **V280 is pending application** — the Supabase connection needs re-auth in this session. The focus-refresh code path works **without** it; applying V280 just makes it instant with no refocus.

Build clean. Next free migration V281.

items.title: fix(discord): auto updating Discord roles does not await for changes to take effect
fix: role changes take effect immediately (refresh session AuthContext per request)
items.body:
## Problem

A user's role/permissions were snapshotted **once**, when their SSE stream was opened (`http.ts` `/sse` handler → `sessionStore.setAuth`). Both the `tools/list` filter and the per-call permission check read that connect-time snapshot for the entire life of the connection.

So when an admin promoted a live user (viewer → editor via `/admin/users`), nothing changed for them: refreshing tools didn't help (it re-lists against the same stale snapshot), and even a client reconnect often didn't help if the client reused the session. Only a full teardown + new SSE session picked up the new role.

### Observed (2026-07-10)
`kcorbett@` was promoted viewer → editor (audit log confirms `admin:add_role editor`, `admin:remove_role viewer`), called `refresh_tools` twice on the same token, and still saw only the read-only toolset. Verified the DB was correct (editor role seeded with `write:*`, her `mcp_user_roles` row attached editor). Root cause was the connect-time snapshot. Worked around in prod by restarting the service (clears the in-memory session store).

## Fix

The bearer middleware already re-resolves the user from the DB on **every** request (`resolveBearer` → `getUserWithRoles`), attaching a fresh `AuthContext` to `req.auth`. This PR writes that fresh context back onto the session in the `/messages` handler, so a role change is picked up on the user's next request. No extra DB call (reuses the middleware's resolve). Legacy bearer requests (no `req.auth`) are untouched.

```ts
// in app.post(MESSAGES_ENDPOINT, ...)
const refreshedAuth = (req as Request & { auth?: unknown }).auth as ...;
if (refreshedAuth) sessionStore.setAuth(sessionId, refreshedAuth);
```

## Client caveat (unchanged, documented)

The server now authorizes writes immediately, but Claude Desktop caches `tools/list` and still needs a connector toggle to *display* newly-permitted tools. Documented in CLAUDE.md.

## Also in this PR (stale-doc cleanup)

- Correct the Lightsail host in `CLAUDE.md`: `44.223.78.200` → `32.193.43.119`; prefer the `lightsail-harness` ssh alias (raw IP has been reassigned before).
- Record that `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED` is now ON in production.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run build` clean.
- Full suite: **732 passed / 11 skipped**. (The global 80% coverage gate fails at 68% — pre-existing on `main`, not introduced here; the transport closure isn't unit-reachable and the integration harness only exercises the legacy bearer path.)
- Post-deploy live check: promote a user and confirm their next tool call reflects the new role without reconnecting (audit log).

items.title: Ensure role changes take effect for active sessions

items.title: [Security] JWT payload embeds full permissions array, so a role change does not take effect until token expiry 7 days later
items.body:
## Describe the bug

`api/auth/login.js` and `api/auth/signup.js` embed the user's full resolved permissions array directly in the JWT payload:

```js
const jwtPayload = {
  id: user.id,
  email: user.email,
  roles: roles,
  permissions: permissions, // full array embedded at sign time
};
const token = jwt.sign(jwtPayload, JWT_SECRET, { expiresIn: JWT_EXPIRES_IN });
```

`JWT_EXPIRES_IN` defaults to `'7d'`. Because permissions are baked into the token at sign time, any server-side role change (demoting an ADMIN to USER, suspending an account, revoking a specific permission) does not take effect until the current token expires. A user who was ADMIN on Monday will continue to hold admin-level JWT permissions until the following Monday.

Since the token blacklist in `logout.js` is in-memory and non-persistent, logging out on a serverless deployment creates a new process with an empty blacklist, re-validating the revoked token immediately on the next request.

## To Reproduce

1. Create a user account and log in. Note the `permissions` array in the decoded JWT.
2. Server-side, change the user's role to USER (lowest permission level).
3. Use the original token to call an endpoint that requires `admin:access`.
4. Observe that the request succeeds because the token still contains `admin:access`.

## Expected behavior

Either the JWT should contain only `roles` (not the full permissions expansion) and every protected endpoint re-derives permissions from roles at request time, or the token expiry should be significantly shorter (e.g., 15 minutes) with a separate refresh-token mechanism.

## Additional context

This is a privilege escalation risk in any multi-tenant deployment where admins can be demoted. The combination of embedded permissions, 7-day expiry, and process-local blacklist means there is no reliable way to revoke elevated access on demand.

items.body:
## Reported symptom

An instance admin creates a user in the instance console, assigns an organization, and checks **Also grant platform admin access**. The resulting account can only operate the instance console — it never gets a working path into its organization workspace.

## Root cause — split-brain org-access storage

Since #693, the session's active org/role, the org switcher, instance membership management, and the SSO guard all resolve org access from `user_organization_memberships`. But several write paths still only touch the legacy denormalized `users.organizationId`/`users.role` columns:

| Flow | What it writes today | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `createInstanceUser` — new identity | `users` row only, no membership | No membership row: invisible to membership-based reads, org switcher empty, instance membership manager says "no membership", SSO works only via legacy fallback |
| `createInstanceUser` — existing identity (#756 path) | membership only — **silently ignores the platform-admin checkbox** | Operator believes they granted platform admin; nothing happened, no error, no audit |
| Org-side `/users` create (`actions/users.ts`) | `users` row only, no membership | Same orphan class as above |
| Org-side role change / deactivate (`actions/users.ts`) | `users.role` / `users.isActive` only | **Does not take effect**: the jwt resolves role from the membership row, which still has the old role |
| Org-side `/users` list (`getOrgUsers`) | reads `users.organizationId` only | Users added to the org via instance-console membership (#756) are invisible to their own org admin |
| SSO guard | memberships → users-column fallback | An org-less platform operator (instance admin with no tenant membership) gets `no_org_binding` and cannot SSO in at all |

## Fix

Make `user_organization_memberships` the canonical org-access store on **every** path:

- [ ] `createInstanceUser` (new identity): create the primary membership in the same transaction
- [ ] `createInstanceUser` (existing identity): apply the platform-admin checkbox with `promoteInstanceAdmin` semantics + audit, and say so in the result message (no silent ignores)
- [ ] Org-side create: insert membership in the same transaction
- [ ] Org-side role change / activate / deactivate: update the membership row in the same transaction (respecting the per-org last-admin guard from `lib/membership-guards.ts`), keeping `users.role`/`isActive` in sync where still read
- [ ] `getOrgUsers`: list via memberships (union with legacy users-column rows so pre-backfill accounts stay visible)
- [ ] SSO guard: allow org-less **instance admins** explicitly (they land on `/instance`; no tenant access implied)
- [ ] Re-run/verify the #693 membership backfill story for existing split-brain rows (pre-production: reseed covers demo)
- [ ] Integration tests for every row of the table above; keep the last-admin guard matrix green

## Use-case matrix that must work end-to-end

1. Instance admin creates new user w/ org + platform-admin checkbox → user lands on /instance, **and** Agency Portal reaches the org workspace, **and** the org admin can see/manage them
2. Instance admin adds an existing identity to another org → org admin sees them; user can switch orgs via the switcher
3. Promote a current org user to instance admin (existing `promoteInstanceAdmin`) → next session shows Platform Console link; org access unchanged
4. Demote an instance admin → org access unchanged
5. Org admin changes a member's role → takes effect on the member's next request (not next backfill)
6. Org-less platform operator → can sign in (local **and** SSO), operates /instance only

Capability: iam-instance-administration
Capability: iam-user-management
Capability: iam-sso-authentication
Persona: Instance Administrator
Persona: CMS Administrator
Related: #693, #756, #758

labels.name: Stellar Wave

items.body:
##  [Security] JWT Role Baked at Login — Role Changes Take Up to 7 Days to Take Effect

### Context
`AuthService.login` signs a JWT containing `{ sub, email, role }`. If an admin changes a user's role in the database, the existing JWT still carries the old role and passes `RolesGuard` until expiry (default 7 days).

### Fix
1. Shorten JWT expiry (e.g. 15 min) with refresh tokens, or
2. Add `tokenVersion` to the `User` entity, increment on role change, validate in `JwtStrategy.validate()`

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Role change takes effect within a configurable window
- [ ] `JwtStrategy.validate()` rejects tokens issued before the last role change
- [ ] Unit test: change role → existing token rejected → new login works

items.title: Changes to application authorizations, groups, roles, and tenants take only effect after re-login

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as a bug

labels.name: severity/mid
labels.description: Marks a bug as having a noticeable impact but with a known workaround

labels.name: component/identity
labels.description: Related to the Identity UI, processing of entities, authentication, or the authorization library

items.body:
### <!-- Component -->

<!-- Identity- -->

### <!-- Affected version -->

<!-- -8.8 -->

### <!-- Severity -->

<!-- Medium- -->

### <!-- Likelihood -->

<!-- High_ -->

### Description

When a user logs in, we determine their associations once (membership in roles, groups, tenants; application authorizations) and put them into the web session.

When these associations change (e.g. user is removed from a group; authorizations change), then this is not reflected in this cached state. Accordingly, as long as the user's session is alive, the changes do not take effect for them.

Examples:
* 1: Groups:
  * I am a member of a group
  * through that group I have the authorization to deploy processes
  * I am removed from the group
  * I can still deloy
* 2: Authorized applications
  * I am assigned to Identity, Operate and Tasklist through an access authorization
  * The access to Identity is removed
  * I can still use Identity
* 3: Authorized applications
  * Authorization checks are disabled for the cluster (leading to authorized applications being populated as `*`, [reference](https://github.com/camunda/camunda/blob/490c1625b75c1f2242ee312c4df076dd98622d79/service/src/main/java/io/camunda/service/AuthorizationServices.java#L76-L80))
  * I have otherwise no application access authorizations
  * I enable authorization checks and restart the cluster
  * I can still access all applications
  * Note: for this we need persistent sessions enabled, as it requires a cluster restart (e.g. on SaaS)

Current workaround: I need to re-login to obtain a new session, at which point my associations are re-evaluated

### Steps to reproduce

See examples in description


### Current behavior

* User associations do not take effect

### Expected behavior

* User associations take effect either immediately or within a reasonable time (that may need to be visible to the end user)

### Environment

SaaS & SM

### Version

- 8.8 since alpha5

### Rootcause

* See `io.camunda.authentication.CamundaOAuthPrincipalServiceImpl.loadOAuthContext(Map<String, Object>)` and related classes

### Solution ideas

* There are different options to solve this:
  * Accept as is (most likely not an option as this can lead to serious user confusion and poses a security issue)=
  * Document it (same reasoning as prior option)
  * Periodically refresh associations for a session; document and/or inform in the UI that changes only have full effect after a certain time; consider making this time configurable
  * Re-check on every request or on-demand when the values are used (probably not viable from a performance standpoint)

### Dev -> QA handover

- Resources:
- Versions to validate:
- Release version (in which version this feature will be released):


### Links

* Slack discussion with serious user confusion: https://camunda.slack.com/archives/C06UYJMMETZ/p1751447255556779?thread_ts=1750440216.996709&cid=C06UYJMMETZ
